title: Cold rebuild: A fail-fast runner
summary: Rebuild A fail-fast runner from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A fail-fast runner** in *Pipelines, stages and artifacts*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Staging passed, so the release job runs `dotnet publish` again and deploys the new output to production. What is the problem?
options: Production gets bytes that were never tested; a dependency or tool may have changed between builds
Publishing twice is slower but otherwise identical
`dotnet publish` cannot run in a release job
steps.explain: Rebuilds can pick up a new package version, a different SDK or a changed environment variable. Promote the artifact you tested.

steps.title: Rebuild A fail-fast runner cold
prompt: Write `List<string> RunPipeline(List<(string Stage, bool Passes)> stages)` that returns one log line per stage:
- `"deploy: skipped"` for every stage after a failure.
Example: `[(build, true), (test, false), (deploy, true)]` → `build: ok`, `test: FAILED`, `deploy: skipped`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<string> RunPipeline(List<(string Stage, bool Passes)> stages)
